verses.1: Praise the LORD. Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good. His steadfast love is forever.
verses.2: Who can recite the mighty acts of the LORD, declare all his praises?
verses.3: Happy are those who keep justice, who do righteousness in every time.
verses.4: Remember me, LORD, in the favor of your people. Visit me with your salvation.
verses.5: That I may see the goodness of your chosen ones, rejoice in the joy of your people, and glory with your heritage.
verses.6: We have sinned with our ancestors, we have transgressed, we have done evil.
verses.7: Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand your wondrous works. They did not remember the abundance of your kindness, but rebelled by the sea, the Red Sea.
verses.8: And you rescued them for the sake of your name, to make known your might.
verses.9: And you rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up, and you led them through the deep as through a desert.
verses.10: And you rescued them from the hand of the enemy, redeemed them from the hand of their hater.
verses.11: And the waters swallowed their enemies, not one of them was left.
verses.12: And they believed your words, sang your praises.
verses.13: But they quickly forgot your works; they did not wait for your counsel.
verses.14: And they longed in the desert for their craving and tested God in the dry place.
verses.15: And you gave them what they asked for, sent plenty into their hearts.
verses.16: And they provoked Moses in the camp, and Aaron, the holy one of the LORD.
verses.17: The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
verses.18: And fire burned in their company, flame devoured the wicked.
verses.19: They made a calf in Horeb and bowed to the idol.
verses.20: And they changed your glory into the image of a grass-eating ox.
verses.21: They forgot the God who rescued them, who had done great things in Egypt.
verses.22: Wonders in the land of Ham, awesome things on the Red Sea.
verses.23: And you said to destroy them. Had not Moses, your chosen one, stood in the breach before you, to turn your anger away from destroying them.
verses.24: And they despised a desirable land, did not believe your word.
verses.25: And they grumbled in their tents, did not listen to the voice of the LORD.
verses.26: And you raised your hand against them, to cast them down in the desert.
verses.27: And to cast down their descendants among the nations and scatter them in the lands.
verses.28: And they joined themselves to Baal Peor, ate sacrifices to the dead.
verses.29: And they incited the LORD with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
verses.30: And Phinehas stood up and interceded, and the plague was stilled.
verses.31: And it was counted to him as righteousness for generation after generation, forever.
verses.32: And they provoked at the waters of Meribah, and Moses was made angry because of them.
verses.33: Because they rebelled against his spirit, he spoke rashly with his lips.
verses.34: They did not destroy the nations that the LORD had commanded them.
verses.35: And they mingled among the nations and learned their deeds.
verses.36: And they served their idols, and they became a snare to them.
verses.37: And they sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons.
verses.38: And they poured out innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters they had sacrificed to the idols of Canaan. And the land was defiled with their blood.
verses.39: And they defiled themselves in their deeds, played the harlot in their practices.
verses.40: And the anger of the LORD burned against his people. He abhorred his heritage.
verses.41: And he gave them into the hand of the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
verses.42: And their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought low under their hands.
verses.43: Many times he rescued them, yet they rebelled in their counsel and were brought low in their sins.
verses.44: And he saw their affliction, heard their cry.
verses.45: And he remembered his covenant, and relented according to the abundance of his steadfast love.
verses.46: And he gave them into the hands of compassion before all who had taken them captive.
verses.47: Save us, LORD our God, and gather us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.
verses.48: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from eternity and to eternity. And let all the people say, “Amen! Praise the LORD!”

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "Not one of them was left" — the Hebrew states that not one of their enemies was left, but the translation reflects the context in which the waters are said to have "swallowed" the enemies.  
- v. 23: "To turn your anger away from destroying them" — the Hebrew uses "to turn back" (שׁוּב) in reference to Moses' intercession, which is rendered here as "to turn your anger away from destroying them."  
- v. 47: "Let all the people say, 'Amen!'" — the Hebrew is ambiguous whether it's the people who affirm the statement or the statement itself ends with an "Amen." The latter is assumed here.
